cs_education_1_texte: It takes place within the structured education system, from pre-school to university.
cs_education_2_texte: It covers educational activities organised outside formal teaching, including extracurricular, after-school and out-of-school activities.
cs_education_3_texte: It comes from everyday learning, at home, in the neighbourhood, through social media and life’s many experiences.
cs_regle_1: Every health club is supervised by at least 3 volunteer teachers.
cs_regle_2: Any properly enrolled student can join the club.
cs_regle_3: Membership is free and voluntary. A list of members must be kept.
cs_regle_4: Once registered, taking part in the activities of the “committees / components / pillars” is compulsory.
cs_regle_5: There is no limit to the number of students in the SOS DOCTEUR TV Health Club.

cs_faq_1_q: Who can join the Health Club at a middle or high school?
cs_faq_1_r: Any properly enrolled student can join the club: membership is free and voluntary, and there is no limit on numbers. The club is open to boys and girls alike, and girls are especially encouraged to join. A list of members must be kept, and every member takes part in the committees’ activities. The club is supervised by at least 3 volunteer teachers.
cs_faq_2_q: How many members must sit on the club committee?
cs_faq_2_r: Every “SOS DOCTEUR TV Health Club” committee has 21 people, with at least 11 girls and at most 10 boys: 1 President, 1 Secretary-General, 1 Treasurer-General and their deputies; 1 coordinator per committee (Pillar 1 to Pillar 7) and their deputies; 1 Adviser.
cs_faq_3_q: Can students with disabilities sit on the committee?
cs_faq_3_r: Yes, absolutely! The committee must be inclusive, in particular by encouraging people with disabilities to take part, and should preferably include more girls than boys.
cs_faq_4_q: Must every secondary school have a club?
cs_faq_4_r: Yes. Under national guidelines, every secondary school (middle and high school) in Togo must have a health club.
cs_faq_5_q: How are the club’s meetings and activities organised?
cs_faq_5_r: The committee holds a regular meeting once a month, and an extraordinary meeting when called by the President or at the request of most members. Awareness activities, clean-up days and educational talks are scheduled outside lesson time to respect the school timetable.
cs_faq_6_q: What do the 3 supervising teachers do?
cs_faq_6_r: The volunteer tutor teachers provide educational supervision, help obtain permissions from the school management, approve the quarterly action plans and help students prepare for competitions and community activities.
cs_faq_7_q: How is a health club officially registered?
cs_faq_7_r: The head teacher sends the minutes of the committee’s installation and the list of members to the Regional Education Directorate (DRE) and to the SOS DOCTEUR TV / AIMES-AFRIQUE national coordination, to obtain the official certificate of affiliation.
cs_faq_8_q: What is the GÉNIE IMHOTEP national championship?
cs_faq_8_r: It’s the national school excellence competition broadcast on SOS DOCTEUR TV, where health clubs compete on general health knowledge, life-saving skills and community impact projects. Official launch of the 1st edition: 2 April 2026.
cs_faq_texte: Everything you need to know to start and run your Health Club smoothly and take part in the championship.

cs_historique_1: In this spirit, the International Association of Physicians for the Promotion of Education and Health in Africa (AIMES-AFRIQUE), founded in Lomé in January 2005 and now present in 20 countries, is stepping up its commitment to education by promoting excellence and healthy competition in schools and universities, as set out in its statutes.
cs_historique_2: As part of its overall mission, AIMES-AFRIQUE launched SOS DOCTEUR TV in August 2020, the first pan-African TV channel dedicated 100% to health. After health, in March 2025 it strengthened its second area of work, “Education”, through the programme “Excellence and Healthy Competition in Schools and Universities in Togo”.
cs_education_texte: Understanding how school, extracurricular activities and everyday learning fit together.
cs_positionnement_texte: The SOS DOCTEUR TV Health Clubs work mainly in non-formal education, offering young people activities that complement school teaching, focused on health, personal development, self-confidence, responsibility and commitment to transformational leadership.
cs_promoteur_texte: It is with immense pride that we see the growing impact of the school Health Clubs in Togo. Our ultimate ambition with this programme is to shape a new generation of civic leaders and public health ambassadors who can take concrete action at school to bring lasting change to the health of our local communities.

axes7_meta_titre: The 7 pillars — Club Santé SOS Docteur TV
axes7_meta_description: The 7 action pillars of the SOS Docteur TV Health Clubs: the slogan and hands-on activities of each pillar, from Génie Imhotep to environmental health.
axe_1_activite_1: Spreading the public health general-knowledge game “Académie Génie Imhotep” to every middle and high school in Togo.
axe_1_activite_2: The “GÉNIE IMHOTEP” national health knowledge competition at municipal, prefecture, inspectorate, regional and national level.
axe_1_activite_3: A weekly GÉNIE IMHOTEP game on SOS DOCTEUR TV.
axe_2_activite_1: E-Club Santé on the SOS DOCTEUR TV app: a space to speak up and talk with health professionals.
axe_2_activite_2: Awareness on Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) and the determinants of health at school.
axe_2_activite_3: Young people’s innovation and creativity in awareness messages, with a yearly collection of good practices.
axe_3_activite_1: Promoting World Health Days (JMS) in schools.
axe_3_activite_2: Rehearsing and producing health sketches, poems, slams, songs and reports.
axe_3_activite_3: “Télé des Ados” shows: weekly broadcasts of club performances by education region.
axe_4_activite_1: Support for physical activities, sports tournaments and inter-club school olympiads.
axe_4_activite_2: Certified training in life-saving skills and emergency first aid.
axe_4_activite_3: Promoting strategy games (chess, Scrabble) and discovering national sports federations.
axe_5_activite_1: PEEP Plus scholarships: 100 yearly excellence scholarships for deserving school-leavers enrolled in health sciences.
axe_5_activite_2: Special quarterly awards for the best supervising teachers and health workers.
axe_5_activite_3: A formal ceremony presenting national awards to winning students and schools.
axe_6_activite_1: Inspiring meetings and direct mentoring with medical figures and non-political opinion leaders.
axe_6_activite_2: “My Word, My Voice Counts” scheme: suggestion boxes and free expression for learners in every school.
axe_6_activite_3: Democratic election of student committees and civic empowerment of young people.
axe_7_activite_1: PEVPAH award (Green, Clean, Sanitised and Hygienic School) for the best high schools.
axe_7_activite_2: Health checks and support for school food sellers to promote healthy eating.
axe_7_activite_3: School tree planting (“1 student, 1 tree”), plastic waste management and water hygiene.

charte_meta_titre: Health Club Charter — Club Santé SOS Docteur TV
charte_meta_description: The rules every Health Club member accepts when creating their account.
charte_1_texte: No insults, mockery, harassment or discriminatory remarks, online or in my club.
charte_2_texte: My nickname is my only public name. It doesn’t contain my full name, my phone number or my email address. The national team may ask me to change it.
charte_3_texte: I never post my contact details or another student’s. My username and password stay secret.
charte_4_texte: Everything I post is reviewed by the national team before it appears. I share verified health information, with no photo of anyone who hasn’t agreed to it.
charte_5_texte: One account per student. Points earned by cheating (multiple accounts, copied answers) are removed, and the account may be suspended.
charte_texte: By creating your account, you accept these rules. They protect every member of the community.
